segments.text: Loupe 1.0: training a page screener on Muse Glimmer.
Loupe has one job: is this page a brand lure? A login or payment form, wearing someone else's brand. Loupe answers first, and Muse Spark takes over when it can't.

The base model is Muse Glimmer on Fireworks AI, with image and text input. We tune it with LoRA, with the vision encoder frozen, through the {fact.serverless}. All of this was read from the provider's model record before any data was built.

The data comes from {fact.accepted} public sets, plus our own renders of popular sites for the benign side. {fact.rejected} other candidates were rejected, mostly for non-commercial or by-request terms. And every file is admitted against its publisher's digest.
For build 1.0 we read {fact.collection} pages, and admitted {fact.admitted}. Most trusted lures are impersonation, then credential pages, with fake shops and payment pages far behind.

A teacher labels the hardest pages first. Muse Spark checked {fact.teacherChecked} South African pages. It agreed on {fact.teacherAgreed} and disputed {fact.teacherDisputed}, and the disputed pages stay out of training and evaluation. That sets the bar: base Muse Spark found {fact.sparkRecall} of confirmed South African lures. Loupe 1.0 has to beat it.

Nothing crosses the split: no shared page, near-duplicate or brand group between training and evaluation. Here's the catch we hit. Grouping by registrable domain chained dozens of brands on one shared host into a single group of {fact.chainGroup} pages. The fix: a domain carrying more than two brands now names a site by its full host.

Two builds were refused by their own checks. Build one kept too few sample-derived lures in training, because shared hosts chained brands into giant groups. Build two came up just short of its {fact.evalPages} evaluation pages, because deduplication dropped teacher-agreed twins. The fix: {fact.build2Fix}.
The recipe is planned: supervised fine-tuning with a LoRA adapter of rank {fact.loraRank}, streamed through the serverless API, for {fact.epochs} epoch.

And a version only ships if it's better. It has to train on more lines than the version before, be measured on the same held-out file, and keep lure recall no lower and false alarms no higher, overall and on the South African slice. Otherwise, the previous version stays.
Serving is planned on {fact.gpu}, scaling to zero when idle. Version names are never reused, and the model card is built only from run records.
The data comes from these public datasets, each under its own licence. Thank you to everyone who published them.
Loupe 1.0 results follow in its model card. The code is on GitHub, at rizonetech slash IsItLegit.
